A cat(1) clone with syntax highlighting and Git integration.

## Key Features ### Syntax highlighting `bat` supports syntax highlighting for a large number of programming and markup languages. ### Git integration `bat` communicates with `git` to show modifications with respect to the index. ### Show non-printable characters You can use the `-A`/`--show-all` option to show and highlight non-printable characters. ### Automatic paging By default, `bat` pipes its own output to a pager (e.g. `less`) if the output is too large for one screen. If you would rather `bat` work like `cat` all the time (never page output), you can set `--paging=never` as an option, either on the command line or in your configuration file. If you intend to alias `cat` to `bat` in your shell configuration, you can use `alias cat='bat --paging=never'` to preserve the default behavior. #### File concatenation Even with a pager set, you can still use `bat` to concatenate files. Whenever `bat` detects a non-interactive terminal (i.e. when you pipe into another process or into a file), `bat` will act as a drop-in replacement for `cat` and fall back to printing the plain file contents, regardless of the `--pager` option's value. ## How to use Display a single file on the terminal: ```bash bat README.md ``` Display multiple files at once: ```bash bat src/*.rs ``` Read from stdin, determine the syntax automatically: ```bash curl -s https://sh.rustup.rs | bat ``` Read from stdin, specify the language explicitly: ```bash yaml2json .travis.yml | json_pp | bat -l json ``` Show and highlight non-printable characters: ```bash bat -A /etc/hosts ``` Use it as a `cat` replacement: ```bash bat > note.md # quickly create a new file bat header.md content.md footer.md > document.md bat -n main.rs # show line numbers (only) bat f - g # output 'f', then stdin, then 'g'. ``` ### Integration with other tools #### `fzf` You can use `bat` as a previewer for `fzf`: ```bash fzf --preview "bat --color=always --style=numbers --line-range=:500 {}" ``` #### `find` or `fd` Preview all search results with `bat`: ```bash find … -exec bat {} + fd … -X bat ``` #### `ripgrep` With `batgrep`, `bat` can be used as the printer for `ripgrep` search results: ```bash batgrep needle src/ ``` #### `tail -f` `bat` can be combined with `tail -f` to continuously monitor a given file with syntax highlighting: ```bash tail -f /var/log/pacman.log | bat --paging=never -l log ``` #### `git` Combine `bat` with `git show` to view an older version of a file with syntax highlighting: ```bash git show v0.6.0:src/main.rs | bat -l rs ``` #### `git diff` Combine `bat` with `git diff` to view lines around code changes: ```bash batdiff() { git diff --name-only --relative --diff-filter=d -z | xargs -0 bat --diff } ``` #### `xclip` Pipe the output into `xclip` to copy file contents: ```bash bat main.cpp | xclip ``` `bat` will detect that the output is being redirected and print the plain file contents. #### `man` `bat` can be used as a colorizing pager for `man`: ```bash export MANPAGER="bat -plman" man 2 select ``` #### Highlighting `--help` messages You can use `bat` to colorize help text: ```bash cp --help | bat -plhelp ``` Or use a wrapper: ```bash alias bathelp='bat --plain --language=help' help() { "$@" --help 2>&1 | bathelp } ``` ## Installation Download prebuilt binaries from the release page for your platform. `bat` is also available through various package managers: - def run(args, inp=b'', env=None):
    e=os.environ.copy()
    # clean
    for k in list(e):
        if k.startswith("BAT_"): del e[k]

    p=subprocess.run(['./executable']+args, input=inp, capture_output=True, env=e)

import subprocess, os
def run(args, inp=b''):
    e={k:v for k,v in os.environ.items() if not k.startswith("BAT_")}; e['PAGER']='cat'; e['BAT_CONFIG_PATH']='/tmp/nope'
    p=subprocess.run(['./executable']+args, input=inp, capture_output=True, env=e)
    return p.returncode, p.stdout, p.stderr
for style in ["plain","numbers","grid","header","header-filename","changes,numbers","full","default"]:

print("file binary no deco but color", run(["--paging=never","--color=always","--style=plain","/tmp/bin.dat"]))
# what about error vs warning stream for file not found etc - that's stderr red

for data in [b"hello\nwor\x00ld\n", b"a"*100+b"\x00", b"\xff\xfe hello\n", "héllo\n".encode(), b"\x1b[31mred\n", b"no null but \xff invalid utf8\n"]:
    open('/tmp/b2.dat','wb').write(data)

def run_tty(args, envx={}, size="80x24"):

    # set winsize via stty in command?
    p=subprocess.run(['script','-qec', f"stty cols 80 rows 24; {' '.join(args)}", '/dev/null'], capture_output=True, env=e)
    return p.stdout

import os, sys, re, shlex, subprocess, json, time, math, difflib
from pathlib import Path

from .data_text import HELP_SHORT, HELP_LONG, CACHE_SHORT, CACHE_LONG, LANGUAGES_TEXT, THEMES_TEXT, DEFAULT_CONFIG, COMPLETION_BASH, COMPLETION_FISH, COMPLETION_ZSH, COMPLETION_PS1
from .themes_data import THEME_PALETTES
try:
    from .data_ack import get_ack
except Exception:
    def get_ack(): return b""

VERSION = "bat 0.26.1 (4dd824a)"
PROG_FALLBACK = "executable"

def prog_name(argv0):
    if not argv0:
        return PROG_FALLBACK
    return os.path.basename(argv0) or PROG_FALLBACK

def eprint_bat_error(msg):
    sys.stderr.write(f"\x1b[31m[bat error]\x1b[0m: {msg}\n")
def eprint_bat_warning(msg):
    sys.stderr.write(f"\x1b[33m[bat warning]\x1b[0m: {msg}\n")

class BatError(Exception):
    pass
class ClapExit(Exception):
    def __init__(self, code, out=b"", err=b""):
        self.code=code; self.out=out; self.err=err

# ---------- languages ----------
def parse_languages(text):
    langs=[]
    for line in text.strip().splitlines():
        if not line.strip(): continue
        if ":" in line:
            name, exts = line.split(":",1)
            ext_list = exts.split(",") if exts else []
        else:
            name, ext_list = line, []
        langs.append((name, ext_list))
    return langs

BASE_LANGUAGES = parse_languages(LANGUAGES_TEXT)
BASE_THEMES = [l for l in THEMES_TEXT.strip().splitlines() if l]

# Unicode width: approximation of unicode_width crate
def char_width(ch):
    if ch == "\x00":
        return 0
    o = ord(ch)
    if o < 32 or (0x7f <= o < 0xa0):
        return 0
    # combining marks
    if o in (0xad,) :
        return 1
    import unicodedata
    if unicodedata.combining(ch):
        return 0
    if unicodedata.east_asian_width(ch) in ("W","F"):
        return 2
    return 1

def str_width(s):
    # s may contain ANSI escapes -> caller strips
    w=0
    for ch in s:
        if ch=='\t':
            w+=1
        else:
            w+=char_width(ch)
    return w

ANSI_RE = re.compile(r'\x1b\[[0-9;?]*[ -/]*[@-~]|\x1b\][^\x07\x1b]*(?:\x07|\x1b\\)|\x1b[@-Z\\-_]')
def strip_ansi(s):
    return ANSI_RE.sub('', s)
def visible_width(s):
    return str_width(strip_ansi(s))

# Rust usize parse errors
def rust_parse_usize(s):
    """Return int or raise ValueError with Rust message"""
    if s == "":
        raise ValueError("cannot parse integer from empty string")

        raise ValueError("invalid digit found in string")
    val = int(body)
    if val > 18446744073709551615:
        raise ValueError("number too large to fit in target type")

{"command":"cat >> app/batpkg/main.py << 'PY'

# ---------- input data ----------
class InputLine:
    __slots__=('content','ending','raw','has_nl','line_no')
    def __init__(self, content, ending, raw):
        self.content=content; self.ending=ending; self.raw=raw; self.has_nl=(ending in ('\n','\r\n')); self.line_no=0

class InputData:
    def __init__(self, kind, display_name, syntax_name_hint, raw, file_path=None, metadata_size=None):
        self.kind=kind  # 'file' or 'stdin'
        self.display_name=display_name
        self.syntax_hint=syntax_name_hint
        self.raw=raw
        self.file_path=file_path
        self.metadata_size=metadata_size
        self.encoding_label=None
        self._detect_encoding()
        self.lines=self._make_lines()
        for idx,l in enumerate(self.lines,1): l.line_no=idx
        self.is_empty=(len(self.raw)==0)
        self.is_binary=self._is_binary()
    def _detect_encoding(self):
        raw=self.raw
        if raw.startswith(b'\xff\xfe'):
            self.encoding_label='UTF-16LE'; self.encoding='utf-16le'
        elif raw.startswith(b'\xfe\xff'):
            self.encoding_label='UTF-16BE'; self.encoding='utf-16be'
        elif raw.startswith(b'\xef\xbb\xbf'):
            self.encoding_label=None; self.encoding='utf-8-bom'
        else:
            self.encoding_label=None; self.encoding='utf-8'
    def _is_binary(self):

# ---------- Printer ----------
def get_terminal_base_width():
    # Try stdout, stderr, stdin tty sizes
    for fd in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr, sys.stdin):
        try:
            if fd and hasattr(fd,'isatty') and fd.isatty():
                return os.get_terminal_size(fd.fileno()).columns
        except Exception:
            continue
    return 80

class PrinterContext:
    def __init__(self, cfg, languages, themes, stdout_is_tty):
        self.cfg=cfg
        self.languages=languages
        self.themes=themes
        self.stdout_is_tty=stdout_is_tty
        # color / decoration booleans
        self.use_color=self._calc_use_color()
        self.interactive=self._calc_interactive()
        self.styles=self._styles_resolved()
        self.term_width=self._calc_term_width()
        # theme resolution (needs truecolor determination)
        self.truecolor = os.environ.get('COLORTERM') in ('truecolor','24bit')
        self.theme_name, self.theme_warning = self._resolve_theme()
        self.theme_palette=palette_for_theme(self.theme_name, self.truecolor) if self.theme_name else {}
        # warn once flag external
        # panel logic later per file
    def _calc_use_color(self):
        mode=self.cfg.color_mode
        if mode=='always': return True
        if mode=='never': return False
        # auto
        if not self.stdout_is_tty: return False
        nc=os.environ.get('NO_COLOR')
        if nc is not None and nc!='': return False
        if os.environ.get('TERM')=='dumb': return False
        return True
    def _calc_interactive(self):
        if self.cfg.decorations_mode=='never':
            # But colour alone? If decorations never and colour always, earlier output had colored plain lines but no decorations - interactive (highlighting) is still True for highlighting (they're distinct). We'll treat interactive as whether printing engine is used (not loop/simple)
            # Determine engine: non-loop if use_color or use_decorations(?) or number...
            pass
        # Engine interactive (vs loop-through/simple)
        if self.stdout_is_tty: return True
        if self.cfg.color_mode=='always': return True
        if self.cfg.decorations_mode=='always': return True
        if self.cfg.force if False else False: return True
        # number flag event last is numbers
        if self.cfg.number_flag_events and self.cfg.number_flag_events[-1][0]=='number' and self.cfg.decorations_mode!='never': return True
        # unbuffered with color/decoration? handled above
        return False
    def _styles_resolved(self):
        # compute styles with auto handling; this uses compute_styles which may raise ClapExit for BAT_STYLE
        styles=compute_styles(self.cfg)
        # auto expansion
        if '__auto__' in styles:
            styles.discard('__auto__')
            if self.stdout_is_tty:
                styles.update({'changes','grid','header-filename','numbers','snip'})
            # else expands to nothing
        if self.cfg.unbuffered:
            # Line numbers automatically disabled; panel removed in unbuffered mode - we implemented by removing numbers (and maybe changes? sample panel 0: changes could still be... there's no file changes in sample. We'll remove numbers only)
            styles.discard('numbers')
        self._styles_raw=styles

    def _calc_term_width(self):
        raw=self.cfg.terminal_width_raw
        base=get_terminal_base_width()
        if raw is None:
            return base
        # raw validated
        if raw.startswith('+') or raw.startswith('-'):
            sign=1 if raw[0]=='+' else -1
            try: off=int(raw[1:])
            except: off=0
            res=base + sign*off
            if res<=0:
                return base
            return res
        else:
            try: v=int(raw)
            except: v=base
            return v if v>0 else base

        opt=self.cfg.theme_opt

        selected=None
        unknown=None
        if opt is None:
            selected='Monokai Extended'
        elif opt in ('dark',):
            selected=dark;

                unknown=selected; selected='Monokai Extended'
        elif opt in ('light',):
            selected=light
            if selected not in self.themes and selected not in THEME_PALETTES:
                unknown=selected; selected='Monokai Extended'
        elif opt.startswith('auto'):

        lines.append(f"> {pager_bin} --version ")
        # output lines - strip trailing spaces? Original outputs command stdout as-is, then blank line then fence
        if out:
            # Remove trailing newline for join logic? We'll append lines from output
            lines.append(out.rstrip('\n'))
        lines.append("```\n")
    except OSError as ex:
        lines.append(f"Could not run command '{pager_bin}': {ex.strerror} (os error {ex.errno})\n")
    # Build text: Original format has blank lines between sections: Our lines entries with \n embedded will produce duplicates. Construct carefully:

    text="\n".join(lines)

    if not text.endswith("\n"):

def jaro(s1,s2):
    if s1==s2: return 1.0
    len1,len2=len(s1),len(s2)
    if len1==0 or len2==0: return 0.0
    md=max(len1,len2)//2-1
    if md<0: md=0
    m1=[False]*len1; m2=[False]*len2; matches=0
    for i in range(len1):
        for j in range(max(0,i-md), min(i+md+1,len2)):
            if not m2[j] and s1[i]==s2[j]: m1[i]=True; m2[j]=True; matches+=1; break
    if matches==0: return 0
    k=0; trans=0
    for i in range(len1):
        if not m1[i]: continue
        while not m2[k]: k+=1

        k+=1
